sentences.text: ----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Nishant Bora For Respondent(s) : Mr. Prem Singh Panwar, PP
Mr. Jamta Ram for complainant  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 12/11/2024

This application for bail under Section 483 BNSS has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.42/2024 registered at Police Station Bagoda,
Dist. Sanchore, for the offences under Sections 363, 376 of IPC and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that as per the prosecution, the petitioner who is aged about 23 years has committed forcible sexual assault/rape upon the victim 'B'.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the statements of the victim 'B' have already been recorded before the competent criminal Court on 31.07.2024 as PW-01.

Drawing attention of the Court towards the statements of the victim 'B', learned counsel submitted that as per the victim 'B', the petitioner captured her obscene photographs and thereafter by threatening her to make them viral, committed forcible sexual assault/rape upon her on multiple occasions.
However, no such obscene photographs have been recovered by the Investigating Agency.

[2024:RJ-JD:45672] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-10634/2024] Learned counsel submitted that as a matter of fact, the victim 'B' entered into a physical relationship with the petitioner out of her own free will and volition.
However, on relations between them turning strained, the petitioner has been implicated in a false criminal case.

It was submitted that since the statements of the victim 'B' have Rafiq Khan vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45672) on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163349635/
1 already been recorded before the competent criminal Court, no fruitful purpose would be served by keeping the petitioner behind the bars for an indefinite period particularly when there is no apprehension of the petitioner influencing the remaining witnesses of the case or tampering with the evidence.

sentences.text:
Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 12.04.2024 and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-petitioner.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application.

Learned counsel for the complainant submitted that the statements of the victim 'B' clearly indicate that the petitioner had subjected her to forcible sexual assault/rape on multiple occasions and, therefore, looking to the seriousness of the accusations levelled against the present petitioner, he does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.

[2024:RJ-JD:45672] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-10634/2024] Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case and after perusing the challan papers so also the statements of the victim 'B' recorded before the competent criminal Court, in the prima facie opinion of this Court, the petitioner is aged about 23 years; the statements of the victim 'B' have already been recorded before the competent criminal Court and, therefore, now there is no apprehension of the petitioner influencing her.

This Court also prima facie finds that the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the petitioner influencing the remaining prosecution witnesses or fleeing away from justice or tampering with the evidence, in case he is enlarged on bail.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 483 BNSS is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Rafiq Khan S/o Gani Khan arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.42/2024 registered at Police Station Bagoda, Dist. Sanchore, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/-
each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 56-divya/-
